changes: The bank point is written for Year 7 in Queensland, South Australia, Western Australia, Tasmania, the ACT and the Northern Territory, so its depth should be checked against the Victorian Levels 7 and 8 content for this course.
The card's examples (steam on a cold window, wax in a pan, water melting at 0 °C and boiling at 100 °C) should be kept or swapped for Victorian-relevant examples if the course prefers local ones.
The card does not mention that each pure substance has its own melting and boiling point, which the new brief requires, so a sentence on this should be added.
match.reason: The bank point covers the same idea of heating and cooling changing states, but it lacks the point that each pure substance has its own melting and boiling point and is pitched for a different state's year level.

confirm.reason: The bank card on changes of state covers melting, boiling, condensing and freezing. This brief also needs sublimation and the idea that each pure substance has its own melting and boiling point, and adding that content goes beyond a small change.

draft.title: Changes of state
card: Heat gives particles more energy, so they move faster. Cooling takes energy away, so they move more slowly.
When a solid is heated enough, its particles break free of their fixed places and it melts to a liquid. Heated further, the liquid boils to a gas.
Some solids turn straight into a gas without becoming a liquid first. This is called sublimation. Dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) does this.

Cooling reverses each change: a gas condenses to a liquid, and a liquid freezes to a solid. Each pure substance has its own melting point and boiling point. Pure water melts at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C at sea level.
draft.remember: More energy lets particles break free and change state. Cooling reverses it, and each pure substance has its own melting and boiling points.

a.q: Ice is heated and melts to water. What has happened to the particles?
opts: They gained energy and broke free of fixed places
They gained energy and changed into new particles
They lost energy and moved closer together
They stayed the same and the ice just got smaller
a.why: Heating gives the particles more energy, so they leave their fixed places and can move around as a liquid. They are still water particles, so the substance has not changed into something new.
a.clue: Does heating add energy or take it away?

b.q: Sam heats a pure liquid and it boils at 78 °C. He heats pure water and it boils at 100 °C. What does this show?
opts: Each pure substance has its own boiling point
The first liquid had more energy to start with
Water particles are larger than the other particles
The liquids boiled at different times of day
b.why: Each pure substance has its own boiling point, so two different pure liquids boil at different temperatures. The difference is not because one liquid had more energy to begin with, since both were heated until they boiled.
b.clue: Think about what is special to each pure substance.

a.best: They gained energy and broke free of fixed places

b.best: Each pure substance has its own boiling point
